reviewTitle: Very tricky application and uneven fading
reviewDescription: This is an okay product. I wanted to love it. It looked so fun, and I was looking for a long lasting lip option to wear to my wedding...but for me, it was definitely not as long lasting as marketed, and they DEFINITELY need to do a much better job of explaining how to successfully apply the product. Pros: -did not feel as drying to me as other long lasting lip options. When you remove the purple mask, it feels like you're not wearing anything. I didn't test how it performs with a balm on top -it is transfer proof once applied properly and dry -the colors are beautiful and interesting. Cons: -Super tricky application. Not sure how people are saying "you just wipe off" the purple part and it's so easy. First of all, you need to apply thickly, evenly, and gently because the product starts to dry and lift with additional brush strokes as you're applying. So you have to be careful not to lift the product off as you're continuing to coat your lips. You also have to try and stay within the lip, which is somewhat challenging with the brush and if you have the rest of your makeup done, you might have to go back and clean up the purple a little bit around your lips. Then once you manage to have a thick even coat of product on, you let it dry. The dry time is a bit unclear to me with some people saying you can leave it on longer if you want a deeper/more intense color. I just left it on til I felt it was completely dry. You should also try to avoid smiling or moving your lips around too much with the purple mask on, because it will crack and that can create unevenness, I've found. Once it's dry, you can't just "wipe it off with a damp cloth." When I did that, I scrubbed patches of the stain off. Because you have to use enough force to remove the pesky dried up purple, but when you do that, you lift off the stain! Plus when you remove it this way, you're more likely to stain your fingers. If you want an even, beautiful result, my advice is to use damp Q tips. Once you're ready to remove the purple, run a Q tip under the sink for a second (the head has to be completely soaked) and then gently and precisely remove the mask. The Q tip should feel like it's gliding very easily and wetly across your lips with just enough even pressure to lift the purple, not scrubbing. Your lips should be wet. I've found that the Q tip allows you to be precise in removing all the pesky purple flecks, and you get the most even result this way without accidentally removing the stain. You'll go through several Q tips but you'll also avoid staining your fingers. Once you're done and your lips are dry, the stain actually looks pretty good and stays that way...until you eat, which brings me to my next point. -This stain won't survive long after a meal. Which is honestly expected. But this would be okay and acceptable if it faded evenly - it doesn't. The stain inevitably grabs onto some areas of your lips more than others, at least in my experience. And so when it starts to fade, you inevitably get patchiness. But then when you try to remove it, to avoid walking around looking like Aunt Gladys - it won't come off easy...which brings me to my next point -for me, the stain seems to grab really strongly onto the wet-dry boundary of my lower lip, creating a sort of stained line across the middle of my lower lip that won't come off for a couple days. I tried micellar water and aquaphor and then gave up caring. It's been slowly coming off. I wonder if this happens because I tend to nervously bite the skin in that area, which probably creates some long term irritation that the stain grabs onto more easily. So just something to keep in mind. All in all...the bottom line is that, despite my review this can be a great product, if you're willing to go through the hassle, if you love the color, and if you're not eating. I would have given this 3 or 4 stars if it faded evenly and weathered a meal a little bit better.

Milani Stay Put Infinite liquid eyeliner truly lasts all day on my waterline (over 12 hours as advertised) without flaking or smudging, and I’m hoping it will never be discontinued again. It will take a bit of getting used to to apply a liquid eyeliner on your waterline, but it’s a game changer! reviewTitle: Caused Allergic Swelling + Zero Gray Coverage = Worst of Both Worlds
reviewDescription: I rarely leave reviews, but after my experience with Keracolor Color + Clenditioner, I felt compelled to share a detailed warning. I have a history of reactions to most hair dyes and color products. Many succeed at coloring my hair but trigger allergic responses. Gentler options like pure hennas often cause no reaction but fail to deliver meaningful color or gray coverage. I hoped Keracolor — marketed as a gentle, conditioning color-depositing treatment — would be a safe middle ground. Unfortunately, it was the opposite. What happened: I applied the product to wet hair, lathered it in, left it on for the full 20 minutes as directed, rinsed thoroughly, and followed with baby shampoo. Within a short time, I experienced noticeable swelling in my cheeks, scalp, and lips. The reaction was uncomfortable enough that I immediately took an antihistamine. The swelling eventually subsided, but it was alarming and completely unexpected from a "clenditioner" type product. On top of the reaction, it provided zero improvement in gray coverage. My hair looked exactly the same afterward — the same amount of gray remained, with no visible toning or deposit. To make matters worse, my hair felt noticeably drier and more brittle than before, despite the product's heavy conditioning claims and added oils (like coconut, shea, and keratin). This was truly the worst combination: an allergic reaction + no results + added dryness. I threw the bottle straight in the trash. For context, I’ve found only one product that consistently works well for me: Naturtint Permanent Hair Color. It delivers excellent, lasting gray coverage while causing no allergic reaction in my experience. It’s the sole exception I’ve found after trying many options over the years. If you have sensitive skin, a history of reactions to hair products, or significant gray hair you actually want to cover, I strongly recommend skipping Keracolor. Always do a patch test with any new product, even those labeled as gentle. There are better alternatives out there for people like me.

reviewTitle: Mocha permanently dyes blonde hair green!
reviewDescription: Mocha turned my highlighted blonde hair green permanently. This garbage will ruin $1000's worth of highlights in 2 minutes flat. If you like playing with fire and decide to try it anyway, here's what you'll need to do when you end up with shades of olive and chartreuse like I did. You'll have to use Paul Mitchell Shampoo Three and leave it in for about 20 mins, then do it again for a second wash... and after about 3 times of doing this double-shampoo on the daily, your hair will finally look light gray instead of like putrid swamp water. Don't even bother with trying dandruff shampoo, clarifying shampoo, apple cider vinegar, or baking soda (or any combo thereof) to lift the green; it's as effective as trying to put out fire with bubblegum. After using PM Three, you'll need Garnier Color Reviver 5-Minute Mask (I used Golden Blonde to counteract the lingering minty gray cast) at least twice in a row. You'll also need a leave-in conditioner or combing cream to cope with all the dryness your hair now has before you can blow it dry. But the fun doesn't stop there. Once dry and styled, you'll then have to use L'Oreal Magic Roots Spray in Dark Blonde and Golden Brown on your dry hair to get your hair to look normal again, and use it all over your hair at that (while trying to not get it all over your bathroom, your body, and everything else you own.) You'll need to top it off with a very light shine spray to get rid of the dullness caused by the root magic. I use Kenra's and it works wonders. And if you don't want a sticky, stiff mess glued to your head the next morning when you wake up, you now get to shampoo the whole thing out before going to bed. And to deal with all the drying chaos you hair has been going through, by now you'll need a deep conditioner along the lines of Kerastase or Shu Uemura. Both are tremendously expensive, but the dryness will be that severe. If going through all this expensive, tedious craziness on the daily doesn't sound like a bowl of laughs, stay away from Keracolor. Trust.

reviewDescription: I chose this product because basically I'd highlighted and been a lighter blonde for summer, went back to ashy blonde for fall (my natural) to match my roots and have a red tone to my hair (I was born super strawberry blonde and it gradually darkened to a darker blonde but in summer will still shine a bit red from natural highlights). It smelled fine, made my hair ultra soft, but basically just made like three spots of my hair super red and it looked awful. I figured initially this might be my bad, read around, split my hair into sections like traditional dyeing, wet and went section to section root to tip, (did not re-dye the super red patches lol) let it all rest in for a bit, showered, towel and air dried only to find it looking nearly the exact same it had before with no color changing the appearance of my roots, the tips of my hair, and being very patchy in the way the color deposited. I did not start this with patchy colored hair or areas lighter and darker than others in ways that this distribution would make sense, and I did take the time to methodically apply to every section of hair and comb it through to ensure total coverage, it simply did not work. It was also very easily washed out and toned down in one purple shampoo wash and another plain shampoo wash, so it isn't like it ruined my hair, but it did give me hope I'd have more a strawberry blonde (the box shows like here's my blonde, here's what it will look like after) and it certainly did not live up to that. The only reason I would buy this would be the same reason people buy wash out dyes and maybe if someone has shorter hair it's less patchy (mine is like an inch below my shoulder) and maybe the other colors people have reviewed are better but I do not recommend this for the strawberry blonde/keeping red/restoring red that it tries to say it can help.
